question: Since the Digital Services Act entered into full effect in February 2024, all platforms are obliged to submit data on their content moderation decisions. Up to now, only very large online platforms (VLOPs) have been adding to the Digital Services Act Transparency Database. 1.
What is the current onboarding status of the online platforms that do not qualify as VLOPs?

What are the reasons for this delay and when does the Commission expect the statements of reasons of all online platforms, not only VLOPs, to be made available in the Digital Services Act Transparency Database?
answer: According to Article 56 of the Digital Services Act (DSA) (1), the exclusive powers to supervise and enforce the DSA vis-à-vis online platforms that have not been designated as Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs) are with the Digital Service Coordinators (DSCs) of the Member States in which these platforms have their main establishment.

As such, for each non-VLOP online platform, the DSC of their main establishment is responsible for the online platform’s registration to the DSA Transparency Database. Without being onboarded by their DSC, no access to the DSA Transparency Database can be granted to a non-VLOP online platform.

Currently, one non-VLOP platform is actively submitting to the DSA Transparency Database, while 30 non-VLOP platforms have been onboarded by their DSCs and are completing a testing of their submission systems in a sandbox environment of the DSA Transparency Database.

Once testing is complete, they will move to the production environment of the DSA Transparency Database and start submitting their statements of reasons. More details on the onboarding process can be found in the DSA Transparency Database documentation page (2).

Due to the large number of platforms that need to be onboarded by their DSCs and the fact that some Member States are still in the process of appropriately establishing their DSCs after the 17 February 2024 deadline, the onboarding process of non-VLOP platforms will likely continue for the next few months. The Commission is working with the DSCs of Member States to onboard non-VLOP platforms as quickly as possible.

The Commission has also opened infringement procedures against six Member States which were either late in designating their DSCs or have not complemented their designations with sufficient empowerments (3).
